title: Regulatory Leadership and Strategy
summary: An eight-module programme for the authority's leaders on mandate, governance, independence, risk appetite, growth objectives, effectiveness and leading change.
intro: This training programme equips senior leaders of supervisory authorities to govern, steer and lead the regulator itself: turning mandate into strategy, safeguarding independence, balancing growth objectives and leading change with credibility.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip the authority's leaders with the frameworks and judgement to set strategy, govern the institution and account for its performance to government, industry and the public. Participants leave able to translate mandate into priorities, set the regulator's own risk appetite, weigh growth and competitiveness objectives against safety and integrity, and lead organisational change.
sections.What It Covers: Mandate and strategy, governance of the authority, operational independence and accountability, the regulator's risk appetite and prioritisation, growth and competitiveness objectives, stakeholder and international engagement, measuring supervisory effectiveness, and leading change.
Intended Audience: Board members, commissioners and executive leaders of supervisory authorities
Heads of department and senior managers responsible for strategy, resourcing and supervisory priorities
Strategy, governance, international affairs and board secretariat staff supporting the authority's leadership
Learning Objectives: Explain how a statutory mandate and its primary and secondary objectives translate into strategy
Evaluate the authority's own governance, independence and accountability arrangements
Set a risk appetite for the regulator and prioritise supervisory work under resource constraints
Assess how growth and competitiveness objectives can be pursued without compromising safety and integrity
Design stakeholder, international engagement and effectiveness measures that build credibility
Lead organisational change and produce a strategic action plan for the authority
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day leadership programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a briefing on international good practice with case studies, facilitated discussion and leadership exercises, and modules can be selected or tailored to the authority's needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Senior management experience in a supervisory authority or public body is helpful. No specialist background in strategy or governance is required.
Core Reading: OECD, Best Practice Principles for Regulatory Policy: The Governance of Regulators (2014)
IMF, The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08, 2010)
IMF, Good Supervision: Lessons from the Field (Working Paper WP/23/181, 2023)
Basel Committee, Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision (2024)

modules.title: From Mandate to Strategy
modules.summary: How a supervisory authority interprets its statutory mandate, ranks its primary and secondary objectives, and turns them into a credible strategic plan and work programme.
objectives: Interpret a statutory mandate and the hierarchy of its objectives
Explain the role of strategic planning in a supervisory authority
Align strategy with mandate, international standards and public expectations
syllabus: Interpreting statutory objectives: primary, secondary and implicit duties
IOSCO and Basel principles relating to the regulator
Strategic planning frameworks for public authorities
From strategy to annual business plan and work programme

modules.title: Governance of the Authority: Board and Executive
modules.summary: The governance structures and practices that support sound decision-making within the authority's own board and executive, and the governance risks specific to public regulatory bodies.
objectives: Distinguish the roles of the board and the executive in a supervisory authority
Assess board effectiveness against recognised good-practice criteria
Identify governance risks such as capture, groupthink and conflicts of interest
syllabus: Governance models for regulatory bodies and how they differ from corporate boards
Board composition, skills, independence and committee structures
Decision rights, delegation and executive accountability
Case study: a governance failure inside a regulator

modules.title: Operational Independence and Accountability
modules.summary: The legal and institutional foundations of supervisory independence, the subtle threats it faces in practice, and how accountability and transparency reinforce rather than weaken it.
objectives: Explain the rationale and legal foundations of operational independence
Assess threats to independence, from political pressure to budget leverage
Formulate a response to a scenario challenging the authority's independence
syllabus: International standards on regulatory independence and adequate resources
Threats in practice: political pressure, industry capture, funding leverage
Accountability to parliament, government and the public as a safeguard
Case study: defending independence under pressure

modules.title: The Regulator's Risk Appetite and Prioritisation
modules.summary: How the authority defines the risks it will and will not tolerate, accepts that a non-zero-failure regime is inevitable, and allocates scarce supervisory resources accordingly.
objectives: Define a risk appetite for the authority and its tolerance for firm failure
Apply risk-based prioritisation to supervisory coverage and resourcing
Evaluate trade-offs between breadth and depth of supervision
syllabus: The non-zero-failure regime and communicating it honestly
Drafting the authority's risk appetite and tolerance statements
Budget, headcount, specialist skills and value for money
Exercise: prioritising a supervisory risk register under constraints

modules.title: Growth, Competitiveness and Secondary Objectives
modules.summary: How authorities with growth, competitiveness or market development objectives can support a thriving financial sector while preserving safety, consumer protection and market integrity.
objectives: Explain the rise of growth and competitiveness objectives for regulators
Assess where growth objectives align with, and conflict with, primary objectives
Identify regulatory levers that support growth without lowering standards
syllabus: Secondary objectives on growth, competitiveness and market development
Proportionality, speed of authorisation and regulatory burden as growth levers
Innovation, market access and international attractiveness
Guarding against capture and a race to the bottom

modules.title: Stakeholder and International Engagement
modules.summary: How the authority maps and manages expectations of government, industry, consumers and international peers, communicates its strategy, and engages with standard-setters and cooperation frameworks.
objectives: Map stakeholder expectations and balance competing demands
Communicate strategic priorities clearly to internal and external audiences
Identify practical steps to strengthen the authority's international engagement
syllabus: Stakeholder mapping: government, industry, consumers, media and peers
Strategic communication, public reporting and transparency
Engagement with IOSCO, BCBS, FSB and other standard-setters
Resourcing international engagement in a smaller authority

modules.title: Measuring Supervisory Effectiveness
modules.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' skills in designing and using metrics that meaningfully measure supervisory effectiveness and outcomes, drawing on approaches used in international assessments such as IMF/World Bank Financial Sector Assessment Programs (FSAPs).
objectives: Explain why measuring supervisory effectiveness is difficult
Describe approaches used in international assessments such as FSAPs
Distinguish output metrics from outcome metrics
Design a balanced set of effectiveness metrics for a supervisory function
Evaluate the risks of poorly designed metrics
syllabus: Why supervisory effectiveness resists simple measurement
Output metrics versus outcome metrics
The risk of measuring what's easy rather than what matters
International approaches: FSAP assessment methodology
Facilitated discussion: metrics currently used in participants' own authorities
Distinguishing output, process and outcome metrics
Balancing quantitative and qualitative indicators
Benchmarking against international peers
Avoiding perverse incentives from poorly designed metrics
Group exercise: design a balanced metrics scorecard for a supervisory function
Common metric design failures
Gaming and unintended consequences of poor metrics
Case study: a metrics framework and its unintended effects
Case study: critique a sample metrics framework and propose improvements
Recap: measurement challenges, metric design, risks
Reflection and discussion
Q&A

modules.title: Leading Change in the Authority
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a leadership plan for change, covering culture, capability, transformation programmes and the authority's response to new risks and expectations.
objectives: Assess the authority's readiness and capacity for change
Apply change leadership techniques to a supervisory transformation
Produce a strategic action plan for the authority
syllabus: Leading cultural and organisational change in a public authority
Building supervisory capability, talent and succession
Managing transformation: technology, structure and new mandates
Workshop: the authority's three-year strategic action plan

related.title: Management and Leadership for Supervisors
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving new and developing managers in supervisory authorities the practical skills to lead teams and make sound decisions.

related.title: Assessing Board Effectiveness
related.summary: An eight-module programme showing supervisors how to assess how a board really works, from papers and decisions to culture and challenge, culminating in case-study interviews.

related.title: Asset Recovery: Tracing, Freezing and Confiscation
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping practitioners to trace, restrain, confiscate, manage and return criminal assets, including crypto-assets and assets held abroad.

related.title: Authorisation and Licensing: The Regulatory Gateway
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving authorisation staff a structured, defensible methodology for assessing applications, key individuals, owners and changes at the regulatory gateway.

related.title: Conducting Regulatory Investigations: From Referral to Outcome
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme taking enforcement staff through a regulatory investigation, from referral and powers to compelled interviews, findings and outcome.

related.title: Core Supervisory Skills: Business Models, Governance and Risk Governance Panels
related.summary: A three-day workshop taking supervisors from business model analysis through governance interviews to a risk governance panel, using running case studies and role plays.
